_comment: Copyright Ben Paul Wise. All Rights Reserved. Legends placed by eye (Ben's route, 2026-09-20). Per work folder: the legend rectangle in source pixels, the orientation the legend hexes are printed in, and one swatch per printed legend entry as [name, kind, sheet, x, y, size]. x y is the swatch centre and size its circumradius, read off a gridded crop of the scan; sheet is the id the hexsheet document uses (or will use) for that meaning. Consumed by legend.py DIR --placed legends.json.

BFM_map_redone.note: Terrain Effects Chart printed sideways; the legend hexes are pointy although the map is flat. No BFM sheet exists yet, so the sheet ids are proposals.

BFM_map_1.note: The original GDW printing has no legend, so each kind's swatch is an exemplar hex on the map itself, picked by eye (the style-library case G2 done on the same scan: nothing is borrowed from another print). The sheet ids repeat BFM_map_redone's so the two readings can be compared kind for kind. Clear is the unmarked default in both printings and has no swatch.

Target_Leningrad_map.note: No printed legend. Exemplar hexes named by printed id (the lattice is numbered), read from a gridded overview on 2026-09-21; the contact sheet is the check. Stars and crosses (set-up glyphs) and the red Leningrad perimeter are left out until the terrain reads. Sheet ids are proposals. 2026-09-21 second look at the contact sheet: 0305 is coastal land, the sea exemplar is 0206; the Lake Peipus hex ids could not be read with confidence, so Lake is left out. Third look: the fortification boxes sit on hexsides (side-mid, exemplar 1506), city pictograms sit in the upper half under the id (glyph-slot), 0708 has forest mottle that outvoted its river (0609 instead), 1203 is half lake (rough exemplar 1803).

Battle_of_Tannenberg_game_map.note: Terrain Key, three columns; the nine fills, glyphs and rings are where the finder found them, the line rows below (river, major river, blocked hexside; single- and double-track railroad; political boundary) placed by eye at the same column centres and a 110 px row pitch. Off-map railroad, reinforcement letters left out. Sheet ids are proposals.

Stalin_Moves_West_map.note: Two columns of eight; the earlier --panel rectangle stopped at y 340 and so missed Front Line and Forest. Sheet ids are those of stalin-moves-west.xml (terrain and line ids; the four glyphs are its symbol names).
